newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index up on rebound after MFN move.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index up on rebound after MFN move.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended Tuesday higher on a rebound after U.S. President Bill Clinton said he planned to renew China's most favoured nation (MFN) trade status, traders said.
The foreign currency B index closed at 169.39 points, up 2.53 or 1.52 percent although turnover shrunk further to HK$87.3 million from Monday's thin HK$105.9 million.
"The B index rallied in the morning on the MFN announcement, but some of the effect wore off in the afternoon," a trader at J&A Securities said.
The B index, which began a rebound on Monday, soared more than three percent in the morning after Clinton announced he intended to extend China's MFN trade privileges for another year.
But profit-taking in the afternoon and simmering rumours of fresh government moves to cool the securities markets ate away some of the gains, traders said.
"Traders were glued to their trading terminals after hearing rumours that the government may extend the settlement period," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

There was talk that Beijing will soon extend the stock transaction settlement period to three days from the current one day for A shares and immediate settlement for B shares to stem stock speculation, brokers said.
Officials at the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the country's top securities watchdog, declined comment.
"Today's small turnover is unlikely to support a bull run, and I think the index will hover at current levels in the coming sessions," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
The domestic currency A share index powered ahead and gained 14.40 points or 3.05 percent to 486.83 on turnover of 9.4 billion yuan against Monday's 6.7 billion.
"The A share market was stunned by Shenzhen Development Bank's roaring success, especially after announcing it was investigating stock trading irregularities," the J&A analyst said.
Shenzhen Development Bank Co, which was suspended on Monday morning after saying it might have been involved in irregularities in stock trading, hit its 10 percent limit-up at 40.67 yuan.
In the B share market, property developer China Vanke Co Ltd was the top gainer, rising HK$0.45, or 5.23 percent, to HK$9.05.
